_about: Fix recipes per rule and stack (P1.3). Used by app/agent/fix_prompt.py and the fix pull request (app/github.py), no model call. Keys under rules are rule ids or fnmatch patterns. A recipe with `header` gets its per-host snippet generated from HEADER_TARGETS in fix_prompt.py. steps: framework, then hosting, then backend, then '*'. {url} and {origin} are filled in from the report. manual: dns, hosting, email or provider; a recipe with only manual text goes to the manual list.

sec.hsts.missing.why: Without HSTS a visitor's first request can be downgraded to plain http on a hostile network, so logins and cookies can be read.
sec.hsts.missing.risk: Only add includeSubDomains when every subdomain serves https; browsers then refuse plain http on all of them for two years.

sec.hsts_*.why: A short, invalid or disabled HSTS header leaves visitors open to downgrade attacks between visits.
sec.hsts_*.risk: Replace the existing Strict-Transport-Security header rather than adding a second one. includeSubDomains needs https on every subdomain.

sec.no_content_security_policy.why: A Content Security Policy is the main defence that stops injected scripts from running if an XSS bug slips in.

header.name: Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only
header.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'

sec.no_content_security_policy.risk: Starts in report-only mode on purpose: a strict policy can block your own scripts, analytics or fonts. Watch the browser console for violations for a few days, add the sources you trust, then rename the header to Content-Security-Policy.

sec.content_security_policy_is_report_on.why: A report-only policy only logs violations; it does not block injected scripts.

header.name: Content-Security-Policy
header.value: <your current report-only policy, once the console shows no violations>

sec.content_security_policy_is_report_on.risk: Switch only after the report-only policy has run without violations you did not expect; otherwise real features break.

sec.csp_*.why: This weakens the Content Security Policy, so an injected script could still run.
sec.csp_*.change: Tighten the existing Content-Security-Policy where it is set. Remove 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' from script-src (use nonces or hashes for the inline scripts you need), replace * or https: in script-src with the exact hosts you load from, and add object-src 'none' and base-uri 'self' if they are missing.
sec.csp_*.risk: Tightening script-src can break inline scripts, analytics or third-party widgets. Ship it as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first and watch the console.

sec.no_x_content_type_options.why: Without nosniff, browsers may guess a file's type and run an uploaded or mislabelled file as script.
sec.no_x_content_type_options.risk: Very low: files must be served with their correct Content-Type, which every modern host does.

sec.no_referrer_policy.why: Without a Referrer-Policy, full page addresses (sometimes with tokens or ids in them) are sent to every site you link to.
sec.no_referrer_policy.risk: Very low: analytics still see which site a visitor came from, just not the full path.

sec.page_can_be_framed.why: Any site can load your pages in an invisible frame and trick visitors into clicking your buttons (clickjacking).
sec.page_can_be_framed.risk: Breaks embedding your site in other sites. If you embed it on purpose, use Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors with those sites instead.

sec.server_header_reveals_a_version.why: An exact server version tells attackers which known vulnerabilities to try first.

*.snippet:
# nginx
server_tokens off;

# Apache
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
*.note: Hide the version number; the server name alone is fine.

sec.cors_*.why: Your API tells browsers that any website may read its responses, so another site could read a signed-in visitor's data.

nextjs.file: the route handler or middleware that sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin
nextjs.note: Reflect only origins you list; never * together with credentials.

*.file: the API code that sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin
*.note: List the exact origins that need access.

sec.cors_*.risk: Other front ends you run on different domains stop working until you add them to the list.

sec.cookie.flags_missing.why: Cookies without HttpOnly can be read by any injected script, and without Secure and SameSite they travel over plain http and in cross-site requests.

nextjs.file: where the cookie is set (route handler, server action or middleware)
nextjs.snippet: cookies().set('session', value, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax', path: '/' })
nextjs.note: Only cookies that browser JavaScript must read may skip httpOnly.

supabase.snippet:
// With @supabase/ssr the auth cookies are set by the library: pass cookieOptions
createServerClient(url, key, { cookies, cookieOptions: { secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' } })
supabase.note: Check which cookie the report names; third-party cookies are set by that provider.

*.file: where the cookie is set on the server
*.snippet: Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
*.note: Only cookies that browser JavaScript must read may skip HttpOnly.

sec.cookie.flags_missing.risk: Code that reads the cookie from JavaScript (document.cookie) stops seeing it once HttpOnly is set.

sec.mixed_content.why: Resources over plain http on an https page can be swapped by anyone on the network, and browsers block some of them.
sec.mixed_content.change: Change every http:// address the report lists to https:// (or a relative path) in your templates and content.
sec.mixed_content.risk: A resource whose server has no https stops loading; host a copy yourself.

sec.*_in_a_javascript_bundle.why: A secret key in a JavaScript file is public: anyone can open the file and use the key with your account.
sec.*_in_a_javascript_bundle.manual_text: Rotate the leaked key in that provider's dashboard now (the old one stays valid until you do), then store the new one only as a server-side environment variable in your hosting settings.

nextjs.file: the file that reads the key, and your env settings
nextjs.snippet:
// Server only: no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, read it in a route handler or server action
const key = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
nextjs.note: Anything named NEXT_PUBLIC_* is copied into the browser bundle.

vite.file: the file that reads the key, and your env settings
vite.snippet:
// Anything named VITE_* ships to the browser. Move the call behind a server function
// (Vercel or Netlify function, or a Supabase Edge Function) that reads process.env.SECRET_KEY.
vite.note: The browser should call your function, never the provider with the secret.

lovable.file: the code that calls the provider
lovable.snippet:
// Move this call into a Supabase Edge Function and store the key with:
// supabase secrets set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=...
lovable.note: Lovable projects are Vite apps: VITE_* values are public.

bolt.file: the code that calls the provider
bolt.snippet: // Move this call into a server function (Netlify or Vercel function) that reads process.env.SECRET_KEY

*.file: the code that uses the key
*.snippet:
// Call the provider from your server with a key read from an environment variable,
// and let the browser call your server instead.
*.note: Publishable or public keys are fine in the browser; secret keys never are.

sec.*_in_a_javascript_bundle.risk: Rotating breaks anything still using the old key; update your server env at the same time.

sec.*_is_publicly_readable.why: Anyone can download this file; config and backup files usually hold passwords, keys or customer data.
sec.*_is_publicly_readable.manual_text: Rotate every password and key the file contained: assume they were copied.

vercel.note: Also delete the file from the public or build folder and redeploy.

netlify.note: Delete the file from the repository's public folder and redeploy.

*.snippet:
git rm --cached .env .env.production *.sql
echo '.env*' >> .gitignore
*.note: Deploy only the build output, never the project root.

sec.*_is_publicly_readable.risk: None to the site; the rotation is what protects you.

sec.source_maps_are_publicly_readable.why: Source maps publish your original source code, including comments and internal endpoints.

nextjs.note: Upload maps to your error tracker instead if you need them.

vite.note: Or 'hidden' to keep them for an error tracker without linking them.

*.snippet: Turn off production source maps (webpack: devtool: false).

sec.source_maps_are_publicly_readable.risk: Stack traces from production get harder to read unless you upload maps to your error tracker privately.

sec.*_has_known_vulnerabilities.why: This library version has published vulnerabilities that attackers can look up.
sec.*_has_known_vulnerabilities.change: Upgrade the library to its latest version (npm install <name>@latest, or change the version in the CDN address), then run your tests.
sec.*_has_known_vulnerabilities.risk: Major version upgrades can change behavior; read the library's changelog for breaking changes.
sec.*_has_known_vulnerabilities.check: npm ls <name>  # or check the version in the <script src> address

sec.library_from_a_public_cdn_loads_with.why: If the CDN is compromised, the script it serves runs on your site with full access.
sec.library_from_a_public_cdn_loads_with.change: Add integrity and crossorigin attributes to the <script> or <link> tag (the CDN shows the SRI hash, or generate it with: curl -s <url> | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A).
sec.library_from_a_public_cdn_loads_with.risk: If the file at that address ever changes, the browser refuses it; pin an exact version in the address.

sec.supabase.public_table.why: Anyone with your public anon key (it is in your JavaScript) can read these tables.

*.file: a new Supabase migration (or the SQL editor)
*.note: Repeat for every table the report lists. With RLS on and no policy, nobody can read it through the API.

sec.supabase.public_table.risk: Pages that read these tables without signing in stop getting data until you add a policy for them.

sec.supabase.public_rpc.why: These database functions can be called by anyone with the anon key.

*.snippet:
revoke execute on function public.<name>(<args>) from anon, public;
grant execute on function public.<name>(<args>) to authenticated;
*.note: Keep anon access only for functions meant to be public.

sec.supabase.public_rpc.risk: Signed-out pages that call these functions stop working.
sec.supabase.public_rpc.check: curl -s -X POST '{supabase_url}/rest/v1/rpc/<name>' -H 'apikey: <anon key>'  # expect a permission error

sec.supabase.public_bucket.why: Anyone can list and download every file in these storage buckets.

*.file: Supabase dashboard, Storage, bucket settings (or a migration)
*.snippet:
update storage.buckets set public = false where id = '<bucket>';
-- then serve files with signed URLs: supabase.storage.from('<bucket>').createSignedUrl(path, 3600)
*.note: Public buckets are only right for files meant for everyone, like logos.

sec.supabase.public_bucket.risk: Public links to these files stop working; switch them to signed URLs.

sec.firebase*.why: Your Firebase data can be read without signing in.

*.note: Then narrow each path to the user who owns it.

sec.firebase*.check: curl -s '<your database url>/.json?shallow=true'  # expect Permission denied

sec.no_caa_record.why: A CAA record limits which certificate authorities may issue certificates for your domain.
sec.no_caa_record.manual_text: Add a CAA DNS record for your domain naming your certificate authority, for example 0 issue "letsencrypt.org" (Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare use Let's Encrypt; Cloudflare also uses Google Trust Services: pki.goog).

sec.subdomain_*.why: A subdomain points at a service you no longer use, so someone else could claim it and serve content on your domain.
sec.subdomain_*.manual_text: Delete the DNS record for that subdomain in your DNS provider, or claim the resource it points at again.

sec.tls_*.why: Your certificate or TLS setup lets browsers warn visitors or lets old, broken encryption through.
sec.tls_*.manual_text: Renew the certificate or turn off TLS 1.0 and 1.1 in your hosting or CDN settings (Cloudflare: SSL/TLS, Edge Certificates, Minimum TLS Version 1.2).

sec.server_negotiates_tls_older_than_n_n.why: Old TLS versions have known weaknesses.
sec.server_negotiates_tls_older_than_n_n.manual_text: Set the minimum TLS version to 1.2 in your hosting or CDN settings.

sec.server_still_accepts_tls_n_n_or_n_n.why: Old TLS versions have known weaknesses.
sec.server_still_accepts_tls_n_n_or_n_n.manual_text: Set the minimum TLS version to 1.2 in your hosting or CDN settings.

sec.http.plain.why: Everything sent to the site, including passwords, can be read on the network.
sec.http.plain.manual_text: Turn on HTTPS and the http to https redirect in your hosting settings (Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare do this for free).

sec.*spf*.why: Without SPF, anyone can send email that claims to come from your domain.
sec.*spf*.manual_text: Add the SPF TXT record your email provider gives you (one record, starting v=spf1).

sec.*dmarc*.why: Without DMARC, receivers do not know to reject mail that fakes your domain.
sec.*dmarc*.manual_text: Add a TXT record at _dmarc.<your domain>: v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@<your domain>

sec.*mx*.why: Without MX records, replies and bounces to your domain are lost.
sec.*mx*.manual_text: Add the MX records your email provider gives you.

geo.robots.blocks_search_bot.why: ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity cannot read your pages, so they cannot quote or recommend you.

nextjs.note: Remove any Disallow for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot.

*.snippet:
User-agent: *
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml
*.note: Remove Disallow lines for OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot. Blocking training bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) is your choice.

geo.robots.blocks_search_bot.risk: Low; if you blocked AI crawlers on purpose, keep the training bots blocked and allow only the search ones.

seo.robots_txt_blocks_all_crawlers.why: Search engines are told not to crawl the site, so it disappears from Google and AI search.

nextjs.note: A staging site should stay blocked; production should not.

*.snippet:
User-agent: *
Allow: /
*.note: Keep Disallow only for private areas.

seo.robots_txt_blocks_all_crawlers.risk: Private pages become crawlable if they were only hidden by robots.txt; protect them with sign-in instead.

seo.no_sitemap_xml.why: A sitemap tells search engines and AI crawlers every page to read.

*.snippet:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url><loc>https://yourdomain.com/</loc></url>
</urlset>
*.note: List every public page and add a Sitemap: line to robots.txt.

geo.no_llms_txt.why: llms.txt is a small map of your site for AI assistants (low measured impact, cheap to add).

*.snippet:
# Your product

> One sentence on what it does and for whom.

## Pages
- [Pricing](https://yourdomain.com/pricing): plans and prices
*.note: Served at /llms.txt from the public folder.

geo.no_llms_full_txt.why: An optional full-text version of llms.txt for AI assistants (low measured impact).

*.snippet:
# Your product

The full text of your key pages, in Markdown.
*.note: Optional.

geo.no_well_known_ai_txt.why: An optional file stating how AI systems may use your content (low measured impact).

*.snippet:
User-Agent: *
Allow: /
*.note: Optional.

geo.no_structured_data.why: Structured data tells Google and AI search exactly who you are and what you offer.

nextjs.snippet:
<script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify({
  '@context': 'https://schema.org', '@type': 'Organization', name: 'Your product', url: 'https://yourdomain.com',
}) }} />
nextjs.note: Static JSON you write yourself is safe here; never put user input in it.

*.snippet:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{"@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "Organization", "name": "Your product", "url": "https://yourdomain.com"}
</script>
*.note: It must be in the HTML the server sends, not added by JavaScript later.

geo.the_homepage_says_little_before_java.why: AI crawlers and many search bots do not run JavaScript, so they see an empty page.

nextjs.snippet: // Keep the homepage a server component (no 'use client' at the top) so its text is in the HTML.
nextjs.note: Move interactive parts into small client components.

vite.snippet:
What your product does

One paragraph for people and crawlers, replaced when the app loads.
vite.note: Or prerender the homepage at build time.

lovable.snippet:
What your product does

One paragraph for people and crawlers, replaced when the app loads.
lovable.note: Lovable apps render in the browser; this text is what crawlers read.

bolt.snippet:
What your product does

One paragraph for people and crawlers, replaced when the app loads.

*.snippet: Render the headline and first paragraph on the server (or prerender them) instead of in JavaScript.

geo.the_homepage_says_little_before_java.risk: Keep the static text identical to what the app shows, or search engines may treat it as cloaking.

geo.page.javascript_only.why: These pages are empty until JavaScript runs, so AI crawlers read nothing.
geo.page.javascript_only.change: Render these pages on the server or prerender them at build time.

geo.your_site_never_states_its_name_in_a.why: Search and AI engines are not sure what your brand is called.
geo.your_site_never_states_its_name_in_a.change: Add <meta property="og:site_name" content="Your product"> to every page's <head>, and a name in your structured data.

seo.missing_meta_description.why: Search engines and link previews show a random snippet instead of your pitch.

nextjs.note: Give each page its own description.

astro.note: Pass a description from each page.

wordpress.file: your SEO plugin (Yoast or Rank Math), page settings
wordpress.snippet: Meta description: one or two sentences, 120 to 160 characters.

*.snippet: <meta name="description" content="One or two sentences, 120 to 160 characters, saying what it does and for whom.">
*.note: Single-page apps: this is the description for every route unless you set it per page.

seo.meta_description_is_too_short.why: A very short description wastes the space search results give you.
seo.meta_description_is_too_short.change: Rewrite the meta description to 120 to 160 characters: what it does, for whom, and why it is different.

seo.page_title_is_too_short.why: The title is the headline in search results; a short one says little.

nextjs.snippet: export const metadata = { title: 'Your product: the one thing it does' }

*.snippet: <title>Your product: the one thing it does</title>
*.note: 30 to 60 characters.

seo.no_canonical_link.why: Without a canonical link, copies of a page (with tracking parameters, www or not) compete with each other.

nextjs.snippet: export const metadata = { metadataBase: new URL('https://yourdomain.com'), alternates: { canonical: '/' } }
nextjs.note: Set each page's own canonical path.

*.snippet: <link rel="canonical" href="https://yourdomain.com/this-page">

seo.no_canonical_link.risk: A wrong canonical hides the page from search; point each page at itself.

seo.no_open_graph_tags.why: Links shared on LinkedIn, Slack or X show no title, text or image.

*.snippet:
<meta property="og:title" content="Your product">
<meta property="og:description" content="What it does">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://yourdomain.com/og.png">

seo.more_than_one_hn_heading.why: Several h1 headings blur what the page is about.
seo.more_than_one_hn_heading.change: Keep one <h1> per page (the page's main headline) and turn the others into <h2>.
seo.more_than_one_hn_heading.risk: Check your styling: some sites style h1 directly.

seo.image.alt_missing.why: Images without alt text are invisible to search engines and screen readers.
seo.image.alt_missing.change: Add a short alt text describing each meaningful image; use alt="" for decorative ones.

seo.broken_internal_link.why: Visitors and crawlers hit a dead end.
seo.broken_internal_link.change: Fix or remove each broken link the report lists, or redirect the old address.

ux.signup_emails_hit_*.why: New users never get their confirmation email, so they cannot finish signing up.
ux.signup_emails_hit_*.manual_text: Set up your own SMTP sender (Resend, Postmark or SES) in your auth provider, for Supabase under Authentication, Emails, SMTP settings, and raise the email rate limit there.

supabase.file: Supabase dashboard: Authentication, Emails, SMTP settings
supabase.snippet:
Host: smtp.resend.com
Port: 465
Username: resend
Password: <your Resend API key, entered in the dashboard only>
supabase.note: Supabase's built-in mailer sends only a few emails an hour and is meant for testing.

ux.signup_emails_hit_*.risk: Emails come from your own domain after this, so its SPF and DKIM records must be set.
ux.signup_emails_hit_*.check: Sign up with a fresh address and confirm the email arrives within a minute.

a11y.control.name_missing.why: Screen readers, voice control and AI agents cannot tell what this field or button is for.

*.snippet:
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" type="email" name="email">

<!-- Icon-only buttons -->
<button aria-label="Close"><svg aria-hidden="true">...</svg></button>
*.note: A placeholder is not a label.

a11y.image.alt_missing.why: Screen reader users hear nothing, or a file name, for these images.
a11y.image.alt_missing.change: Add alt text that says what the image shows; use alt="" for decorative images.

a11y.*.why: This stops some visitors, and AI agents that rely on the accessibility tree, from using the page.
a11y.*.change: Fix the elements the report lists, following the fix line of the finding.

perf.*.why: Slow pages lose visitors, and Google ranks slow mobile pages lower.

nextjs.snippet:
import Image from 'next/image'
<Image src="/hero.jpg" alt="..." width={1200} height={600} priority />
nextjs.note: Use next/image, lazy-load below-the-fold parts with next/dynamic, and keep third-party scripts on strategy="lazyOnload".

*.note: Compress images to WebP or AVIF, size them, lazy-load what is below the fold, and defer non-critical scripts.

perf.*.risk: Lazy-loading the main above-the-fold image makes LCP worse; load that one eagerly.
